title: Plagues of Frogs, Gnats, and Flies

questions.question: What did the second plague bring upon Egypt?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:6 (ESV): "Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt."

questions.question: What did the third plague turn dust into?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:17 (ESV): "All the dust of the earth became gnats in all the land of Egypt."

questions.question: What did the fourth plague bring?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:24 (ESV): "There came great swarms of flies into the house of Pharaoh."

questions.question: What did Pharaoh ask Moses to do about the frogs?
options: Pray to the Lord to remove them
questions.correctAnswer: Pray to the Lord to remove them
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:8 (ESV): "Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, 'Plead with the Lord to take away the frogs from me.'"

questions.question: Which land was spared from the plague of flies?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:22 (ESV): "I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people dwell, so that no swarms of flies shall be there."

questions.question: What did the magicians say when they could not replicate the gnats?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:19 (ESV): "The magicians said to Pharaoh, 'This is the finger of God.'"

questions.question: When did Moses tell Pharaoh the frogs would be removed?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:10 (ESV): "He said, 'Tomorrow.' Moses said, 'Be it as you say.'"

questions.question: What did Pharaoh promise regarding sacrifices after the frogs?
options: To let the people go to sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: To let the people go to sacrifice
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:8 (ESV): "Plead with the Lord... and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the Lord."

questions.question: What condition did Pharaoh put on letting Israel sacrifice during the flies?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:28 (ESV): "Pharaoh said, 'I will let you go to sacrifice... Only you must not go very far away.'"

questions.question: Where did the dead frogs pile up?
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:14 (ESV): "They gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank."

questions.question: Why did Moses say Israelites could not sacrifice in Egypt?
options: Their sacrifices would be an abomination to Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: Their sacrifices would be an abomination to Egyptians
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:26 (ESV): "We shall sacrifice to the Lord our God offerings abominable to the Egyptians."

questions.question: What purpose did God give for distinguishing Goshen during the flies?
options: So Pharaoh may know God is the Lord in the midst of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: So Pharaoh may know God is the Lord in the midst of the earth
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:22 (ESV): "That you may know that I am the Lord in the midst of the earth."

questions.question: What exactly struck Aaron to produce the gnats?
options: His staff struck the dust of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: His staff struck the dust of the earth
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:16-17 (ESV): "Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth... Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust."

questions.question: Where specifically did the frogs go when they left the Nile?
options: Into houses, bedrooms, beds, ovens, and kneading bowls
questions.correctAnswer: Into houses, bedrooms, beds, ovens, and kneading bowls
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:3 (ESV): "The Nile shall swarm with frogs... into your house and into your bedroom and on your bed and into your ovens and your kneading bowls."

questions.question: What did Pharaoh do after the flies were removed?
options: He hardened his heart and did not let the people go
questions.correctAnswer: He hardened his heart and did not let the people go
questions.explanation: Exodus 8:32 (ESV): "Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and did not let the people go."

key_verse_text: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, ‘This is the finger of God.’ But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, as the Lord had said.
